labels.text: The US announces it is tracking alleged Chinese spy balloons over the Americas, later announcing that the balloons did not collect any information. One balloon drifts from Yukon to South Carolina before being shot down the next day, and a second hovers over Colombia and Brazil. This event is followed by subsequent detections and shootdowns of high-altitude objects elsewhere.
The South African Navy hosts a 10-day joint military exercise in the Indian Ocean with Russia and China.
The National People's Congress unanimously re-elected Xi Jinping as the President of China to an unprecedented third term.
Iran and Saudi Arabia agree to resume diplomatic relations which were severed in 2016, at talks mediated by China.
Honduras switches its formal diplomatic recognition of "China" from the Republic of China to the People's Republic of China.
Brazil and China sign an agreement to trade in their own currencies, ceasing the usage of the United States dollar as an intermediary.
India surpasses China as most populous country.
Honduras opens its first embassy in Beijing, China, after breaking off relations with Taiwan in March.
Indian oil refiners start payments for Russian oil imports in Chinese yuan as an alternative to the US dollar due to increasing sanctions against Russia.
Iran joins the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, becoming the organization's ninth member.
China and the Solomon Islands sign a cooperation agreement between the People's Police and the Royal Solomon Islands Police Force in an upgrade of bilateral relations.
The 2022 Asian Games are held in Hangzhou, China in 2023 instead of 2022 due to COVID-19 pandemic.

President Biden hosts the APEC summit in San Francisco, which Chinese president Xi Jinping attends. Both countries, at the conclusion of the summit, agree to re-open suspended channels of military communications and to cooperate in their fight against climate change.
China brokers a unity agreement between rival Palestinian factions Fatah and Hamas to form a single government.
A 7.1 magnitude earthquake strikes Tibet, China, killing at least 126 people, while another 338 are injured.

Global technology shares outside China fall sharply in response to the release of DeepSeek's chatbot, a Chinese competitor to OpenAI's ChatGPT. Chip giant Nvidia loses almost $600 billion of its value, the biggest drop for a single company in U.S. stock market history.
China–United States trade war: China announces export controls and increased tariffs on certain American imports in retaliation for Donald Trump's imposition of tariffs on Chinese goods.
The 2025 World Games are held in Chengdu, China.
The first World Humanoid Robot Games are held in Beijing, China.

Islamic State insurgency in Afghanistan: Seven people are killed and twenty others injured in a bombing at a Chinese restaurant in Shahr-e Naw, Kabul, Afghanistan. The Islamic State – Khorasan Province claims responsibility.
An explosion at a fireworks factory in Liuyang, Hunan, China kills 37 people and injures 51 others.
A gas explosion at the Liushenyu coal mine in Shanxi, China, kills 82 people.
Poland wins the 2026 FIVB Men's Volleyball Nations League, held in Ningbo, China, defeating the United States 3–2 in the final.

2026 Nepal–Tibet floods: At least 1,403 people are killed and 6,650 are reported missing after a landslide and glacial collapse trigger flash floods and debris flows at the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
Flash flooding and landslides kill at least 56 people in India and at least 14 people in Nepal. For Nepal this occurs one month on from devastating floods.
